_notes: This file exists because of DISC-019: this model's materials are called bw00.001, bwfmp,
bwfgd and oyctp, so the nominal cue (C3) contributes almost nothing and the geometric and
material-physical cues cannot tell painted body metal from a painted door skin — nothing
can, from geometry alone. syndicate-prepare reported 74.6% of the triangles unclassified
and ranked the materials responsible; every entry below is copied from that ranking.
Eight names, covering 45% of the model's triangles. That is D15-R9's claim made concrete:
an operator labels tens of things, never the 6,830 shells the separation stage produces.
Everything here is 'chassis' unless the file gave a reason to say otherwise, which is the
correct-if-coarse answer D15-R2 describes: a shell that ends up in the chassis is a shell
in the right place with a coarser slot than it might deserve. Splitting the bodywork into
doors and wings needs regionLabels (D15-R10) and needs somebody to look at the model.
